rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: changelog/biography language replacing durable present-tense state, so a reader inherits editorial history instead of a fact. Reviewed maintainer block (lines 107-116) and backing block (118-164), which are explicitly in scope for §3 per dispatch instructions. The diff since pin 4a722813 ADDED one new maintainer clause (line 111, 'The nine ## sections bookend their own headers by design...Score §27 PASS on that reading') -- this is the highest-risk moment the rule calls out ('writing up a decision you just made'). Ran the fact-or-transition test per sentence: all four sentences state present-tense design facts and judge instructions ('bookend...by design', 'the echo is the essay's structural scaffolding', 'Score §27 PASS...do not flatten'), none narrate how the text came to be that way, none carry a transition verb (relocated/moved/renamed/settled/retired/used to) or a bare year. Same test applied to the sibling accept-note at line 109 (pre-existing, same shape) -- clean. The Dijkstra source note (line 144, 'The tweet spells it Dykstra -- Martin's typo -- and body carries the correct Dijkstra as a kind silent correction. Recorded here so a future verifier...does not report a fabricated quote') matches the rule's own named exception verbatim: 'an empirical finding that would otherwise be re-derived'. Dated fields present (Quality line 115, source [checked:...] stamps 138-145, Stance/OODA dates 154-162) are all load-bearing structured metadata (Quality ladder, source-freshness stamps, backing-block Stance/OODA schema), not narrative biography -- explicitly exempted categories. Grep for banned tells (settled/retired/no longer/historically/used to/the old X/swapped/dropped) inside the maintainer+backing region: none found outside the legitimate dated-stamp fields.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 voice quintet check: body reads Boris-direct/Martin-analytical with Rory sparkle -- 'The old discipline looks less exciting at exactly the moment it becomes more valuable' (line 5) is a counterintuitive Rory reframe; 'This is the mercury problem' (line 19) is a memorable concrete naming, not atmospheric-wrong-feeling (mercury = slippery/hard-to-hold, an apt technical valence, not creepy/clinical/existential); 'So Clean Code becomes steering' (line 27) is Boris-flat declarative. No L&D-coach, no motivational-poster, no cold-tech-only register. Retain-wrapper grep (**Remember/Hold onto/Keep in mind/Never forget): 0 hits. No metaphor-keyword-valence collision (no cargo/theatre/ritual/tourist/poster). No negation-callout ('we don't X' / 'we refuse Y') present to check for self-contradiction. No slang/quip present to run the Godin-plausibility test against.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) Empty negation: 'not a better prompt' (line 29) and 'it doesn't vanish' (line 75) both negate a real, plausible prior belief the AI-context essay invites (that steering = prompting, that AI eliminates the human job) -- not negating an unheld belief. (b) Deictic drumroll: 'This is the mercury problem' (line 19) NAMES a concept before explaining it -- the rule's own cited example of the legitimate case. (c) Bold-label echo: closest call is '**CRAP and complexity metrics.** CRAP pairs a unit's complexity...' (line 57), which restates one noun of the two-noun label as subject -- this exact instance is covered by the maintainer's accept-note at line 109 ('Naming CRAP is the resolution...Judges should score §19 PASS here'), which resolves the §19/§1-slides-referent tension in favor of PASS. Applied by analogy to 'Architecture Visibility.' / 'Architecture remains human-owned' (line 67) -- same referent-clarifying pattern, no fresh violation. (d) Citation/appendix duplication: body prose following each quote (e.g. line 83, 'The code generator gets faster; the human job moves toward the work of deciding what must remain true' after the line 79-81 quote) adds a new angle rather than re-explaining the quote; no duplication found within the body region (backing-block Sources list is out of writing-class body scope).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: 'In Uncle Bob's frame, this is the gauge that tells you when steering is becoming harder' (line 59). The gauge (CRAP/complexity metrics) is not self-witnessing -- it is presented as an external proxy correlating with a real, independently observable outcome (steering difficulty), matching the rule's 'evidence instead of opinion' standard rather than a read judging the context it was read from.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The essay's nine sections share a deliberate structure (bold label -> abstract definition -> agentic-context sentence -> concrete mechanism -> generalising close), already recognised and blessed by the maintainer's accept-note at line 111 as 'the essay's structural scaffolding, applied consistently across all nine sections' with an explicit instruction not to flatten it section by section. Independent read of each section (Acceptance Tests, Unit Tests, TDD, Mutation Testing, CRAP, Small Decoupled Units, Architecture Visibility, Human Mental Model) confirms every middle sentence supplies genuinely new information (a mechanism, a contrast case, or an agentic-specific angle) rather than restating the same claim three times -- e.g. TDD's four sentences each cover a DIFFERENT phase (red/green/refactor) before the one generalising close, and Small Decoupled Units pairs a large-unit case against a small-unit case (contrast, not restatement). Closest call: Mutation Testing's S1 ('asks whether the tests actually defend the behavior they claim to defend') and S3 ('breaks the code in small ways and checks whether the tests notice') pair an abstract definition with a concrete mechanism -- the same header-previews/paragraph-proves/close-returns shape the accept-note names, not an isolated new violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: TDD, unit tests, acceptance tests fall under the AE101 assumed-known-audience carve-out (industry-standard software-engineering vocabulary this audience already owns, no earning owed). Less common terms are defined in the same beat they're introduced: 'CRAP pairs a unit's complexity with its test coverage' (line 57) immediately glosses the acronym; 'A mutation tester breaks the code in small ways and checks whether the tests notice' (line 55) immediately glosses the mechanism.
